221.q1: I slow down and turn left immediately.
221.q2: The tractor has to give way to me.
221.q3: I have to give way to the tractor.
221.q4: The right hand give way duty applies here.
221.e1: No. You have to give way to the tractor. Right hand give way duty applies here.

222.s: You would like to park the silver car here. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?

286.s: You would like to turn to the right here. There is no one behind you in the blind spots. How will you continue?

286.e2: No, there is not enough space.

290.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic light.

290.e3: No, the cyclist is entering the junction and you must not be of inconvenience when turning left.
290.e4: Yes. If there is no light in the 'minus green traffic light', that means that the oncoming traffic still has green light.

291.s: You would like to leave the green car here. What are the rules about using the car lights?
291.q1: I will leave the car without the lights on.
291.q2: I will leave the car with the high beam on.
291.q3: I will leave the car with the low beam on.

292.s: You are driving at 50 km/h. What should you pay special attention to here?

292.q3: I continue at the same or almost the same speed of 50 km/h.

292.e4: Yes, because of the cyclist on you right.

293.e4: No, they have to give way to you.

294.e2: Yes, because of the traffic sign.
294.e3: Yes. You meet the truck in the bend and the road is narrow, so you need to adjust your speed and pay special attention to the road bend.

295.q2: I continue with the same speed at 60 km/h.
295.q4: I pay special attention to possible oncoming traffic further ahead.
295.e4: Yes.  The sign warns you that you can meet oncoming vehicles.

296.q1: I pay special attention to the pedestrian.
296.q2: I pay special attention to the oncoming car.
296.q3: I continue with the same or almost the same speed of 30-35 km/h.

297.q2: I move all the way up to the parked cars on my right.
297.q3: I continue with the same or almost the same speed of 35-40 km/h.
297.q4: I move as much as possible to the right of my lane.
297.e2: No. There is enough space here for you and the oncoming traffic.
297.e3: Yes, there is enough space here for you and the oncoming traffic.

299.e1: No. Stopping or parking is not permitted 5 metres in front of the exit from a cycle path that runs alongside the carriageway and next to a barrier line if the distance between the vehicle and the line is less than 3 metres and there is no dotted line between the vehicle and the barrier line.
299.e2: No. Stopping or parking is not permitted on a stretch of road where the carriageway before an intersection is divided into lanes by means of barrier lines, or within a distance of 5 m before the beginning of such a stretch of road, nor is stopping or parking permitted 5 m before the exit from a bicycle path that runs along the carriageway and next to a barrier line if the distance between the vehicle and the line is less than 3 m and there is no dotted line between the vehicle and the barrier line.

300.s: You would like to park the silver car here. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
300.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
300.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
300.e2: Yes. It is a parking area for cars, but it is also permitted for lorries and buses.

301.s: You are driving at 50km/h and you would like to continue straight ahead. What should you pay special attention to?

302.e1: No, you have to pay special attention to the yellow lines.

303.e4: Yes, you will not be of inconvenience to the cyclist.

305.q2: I pull as much as possible to the left of the road.

305.e3: Yes, the oncoming car is far away.
305.e4: No. There is enough space to overtake here.

306.s: You would like to leave the green car here. What are the rules about using the car lights?
306.q1: I will leave the car with the high beam on.

309.q4: I slow down and wait with overtaking.
309.e1: Yes, you are not allowed to cross the continuous line.

310.s: You are driving at 70 km/h and you have caught up with the vehicles in front, that are driving at 60 km/h. There is a free rear view. How will you continue?
310.q1: I speed up to 80 km/h and overtake both vehicles.
310.q2: I speed up to 80 km/h and overtake only the black car.
310.q3: I continue with the same speed of 70 km/h and overtake the black car.
310.q4: I slow down and stop overtaking.
310.e4: Yes, because of the bad view and the little difference in speed that you are driving as well as the speed of the vehicles you would like to overtake.

311.s: You are driving at 70 km/h outside a built-up area. The car in front of you is driving slower. There is a free rear view. What will you do?
311.q1: I speed up to 80 km/h and overtake the black car right away.
311.q2: I slow down and wait to overtake the car in front of me.
311.q3: I pay special attention to the road markings.
311.e2: No, there is enough space here to overtake.
311.e3: No, there are broken lines here and you are allowed to overtake the black car here.

312.s: You are driving at 80 km/h outside a built-up area. The lorry in front of you is driving 70km/h. There is a free rear view. What will you do?

312.q2: I continue at the same speed of 80 km/h and overtake the lorry straight away.

314.q1: I will drive without the lights on.

315.q2: I pass the pedestrian on her right side right away.

320.e4: No, you should slow down and continue with approximately 20-30 km/h.

§ 15. Drivers must, taking into account other traffic and the conditions in general, keep as far to the right as possible. (typically yes answer to the theory test)
So when driving on the road you should not keep as far to the left as possible but in the middle of your lane and when you answer that you keep as far to the right as possible then it can also mean that you place only 2-3 centimeters to right and it is not the same as: I pull all the way to the right edge of the carriageway, then you have pressed all the way to the right. 619.e2: No. In this situation you have to pay special attention to the pedestrian. Right now you don`t need to pay special attention to the car in front or the blue car coming from the right side.
619.e4: Yes, you have to hold for the pedestrian.

620.s: You are driving very slowly and you would like to turn to the right here. The traffic light has just changed to yellow. There is no one behind you (free rear area). How will you continue?
620.q1: I enter the junction and turn right.
620.q2: I pay special attention to the traffic light.
620.q3: I pay special attention to the reduced road grip.
620.q4: I brake and stop before the stop line.
620.e4: Yes, because you are driving very slowly.

621.s: You are driving at about 25-30 km/h. How will you continue?
621.q1: I pay special attention to the vehicle from the side road.
621.q2: I continue with the same or almost the same speed of 25-30 km/h.
621.q3: I slow down and give way to the car from the right side.
621.q4: I pay special attention to the reduced road grip.
621.e1: Yes. If you cannot see road markings, then you have to give way to traffic from your right side.( right hand give a way duty).

622.s: You are driving at about 25-30 km/h. How will you continue?
622.q1: I pay special attention to the road condition/state of the road.
622.q2: I have to obey the absolute give way duty.
622.q3: I have to obey the right hand give way duty.
622.q4: I look to both sides before I enter this crossroad.
622.e3: Yes. If you cannot see any road markings, then you have to give away to traffic, from your right side.
622.e4: Yes. You have to look, first to the left side and then right, before you enter the crossroad.

623.s: You are driving very slowly. What will you do now?
623.q2: I give way to the black car in front of me, that is turning left and then I will continue straight ahead.
623.q3: I stop and give way to both cars, that are coming from my right.
623.q4: The cars on my right, should give way to me.
623.e1: No. You have to give away to vehicles on your right.
623.e2: No. You have to give away to both cars, that are coming from your right.
623.e4: No. If you cannot see any road markings, then right hand give way duty applies.

624.s: You would like to continue straight ahead at this junction. What should you pay special attention to here?
624.q1: I pay special attention to the black car from the side road.
624.q2: The absolute give way duty applies at this junction.
624.q3: Right hand give way duty applies at this junction.
624.q4: The car from the side road should give way for me.
624.e2: Yes. The black car is crossing the cycleway, and that is why he has absolute give way duty.

625.s: You are driving at about 50 km/h. How will you continue?
625.q1: I pay special attention to the road condition/state of the road.
625.q2: I continue at the same or almost the same speed of 50 km/h.
625.e2: No. You can and must stop the car before the traffic light.
625.e4: Yes, due to the slippery conditions

626.s: You have just left the silver car here. It is 10 AM on Monday. What are the rules about stopping and parking?
626.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
626.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
626.q3: Loading or unloading passengers is allowed.
626.e3: Yes. Because the sub-board indicates that exit and entry are permitted.

627.s: You are driving at 50 km/h. What should you pay special attention to?
627.q1: I am particularly aware of approaching a school.
627.q4: I continue at the same speed.
627.e3: No, there is no one around.

628.s: What should you pay special attention to here?
628.e1: No. This sign is valid only for lorries and buses.
628.e2: Yes. Red indicates that you must stop.
628.e3: Yes. You must turn left from this lane.
628.e4: No. You don’t need to be particularly aware of traffic approaching from behind at this point.

629.s: What are the regulations for a car’s horn?
629.q1: The horn must emit a steady tone.
629.q2: The horn must emit a clear tone.
629.q3: The horn is allowed to emit musical tones.
629.e1: Yes. The horn must produce a continuous tone.
629.e2: Yes. The horn must have a clear tone.

630.s: What should you pay special attention to here?
630.q4: Traffic from the side roads should give way to me.
630.e1: Yes. You are driving on a main road.
630.e4: Yes. When driving on a main road, traffic from side roads must give way to you. Another rule is that outside built-up areas you are not allowed to park on the carriageway, although you may stop.

631.s: You would like to turn to the right here. What should you pay special attention to here?
631.q4: The cyclist from behind on my right.
631.e1: No. You must not turn to the right.
631.e2: Yes. It is the compulsory direction.

632.s: You would like to turn right in this junction. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
632.q1: I pay special attention to the road markings.
632.q2: I pay special attention to the light signal.
632.q3: I have to turn to the left in the junction.
632.q4: I will change my lane right away.
632.e4: Yes. It is free from behind and there are still broken lines.

633.s: You have just stopped the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
633.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
633.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
633.q3: I am allowed to stop the car here for 10 minutes, if I am boarding.
633.e2: Yes. A stop is any leaving of the vehicle with or without the driver for a maximum of 3 minutes.

634.s: You have just left the dark car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
634.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
634.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
634.e1: No. There must be at least 5 meters distance from the end of a cycle path, and 10 meters from the corner of the intersection. (You can see the yellow triangle at the bottom of the picture on the curb, to help motorists judge the distance to the corner of the intersection)

635.s: You have just left the blue van. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
635.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
635.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
635.q3: I am allowed to unload some goods here.
635.e1: No. The car should be parked a minimum of 10 meters from the corner.

636.s: You have just left the red car. It is 5:00 pm on Saturday. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
636.q1: I am allowed to park the car here for 2 hours.
636.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
636.q3: Loading or unloading of passengers is allowed.
636.e1: Yes. Stopping is forbidden only on work days from 9 am to 4 pm and on Saturday from 10 am to 3 pm.

637.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
637.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
637.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
637.q3: Stopping is forbidden before the sign.
637.e1: Yes. Both signs are temporary and the last sign defines the area where stopping is prohibited. (Stopping is prohibited up to the sign).

638.s: You have just left the black car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
638.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
638.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here.
638.e2: No. The car is turned in the wrong direction. It is not allowed to stop the car facing the wrong direction on major roads (notice the bus stop).

639.s: How many meters after the bus stop are you allowed to stop the car?

640.s: You have slowed down to turn right. How will you continue?
640.q2: I pay special attention to the cyclist.
640.q3: I move my foot to the brake.
640.q4: I slowly enter the junction and turn when it is free.
640.e1: No. The cyclist is in motion. Both feet are on the pedals.
640.e2: Yes, the cyclist is in movement. Cyclist`s feet are on the pedals.
640.e3: Yes. When you move your foot to the brake, you are on alert and your reaction time is reduced. You must be prepared to stop if the cyclist continues to run a red light.

641.s: You would like to continue straight ahead at this junction. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
641.q1: I pay special attention to the road markings.
641.q2: I continue straight ahead from this lane.
641.q3: I change my lane right away.
641.q4: I have to turn to the right at this junction.
641.e2: No. Only buses may continue straight ahead from this lane.
641.e3: Yes. It is free from behind.
641.e4: No. You can still change your lane.

642.s: You are holding still and would like to turn right. There is no traffic from behind. How will you continue?
642.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic lights.
642.q2: I pay special attention to the cyclist.
642.q3: I slowly enter the junction right away and turn when it is free.
642.q4: I will wait until the traffic light changes to green, before I turn right.
642.e1: Yes, there is a green arrow.
642.e2: Yes. One of the cyclists is moving.
642.e4: No, there is a green arrow for you.

643.s: You would like to continue straight ahead. What will you be particularly aware of here?
643.q2: I am particularly aware of the pedestrians.
643.q3: I am particularly aware of driving in a residential area.
643.q4: I am particularly aware of the junction further ahead.
643.e1: No, the road is in a good condition.
643.e2: Yes, you are passing a stadium with a lot of people.
643.e3: No, it is not a special type of road. (there are no signs or road markings that indicate this)
643.e4: No, for now you need to be aware of what is closer to you.

644.s: At what speed will you drive after these signs?
644.e4: Yes. The last sign shows you exit a built up area and maximum allowed speed after this sign is 80 km/h.

645.s: What does the posture of the home guard indicate?
645.q1: I may continue straight ahead in this junction.
645.q2: I may turn left in this junction.
645.q3: I may turn right in this junction.
645.q4: I have to stop and wait for the home guard officer to give a sign before I continue driving.
645.e4: Yes. The posture of the home guard officer here means that you have to stop, (If you can see the back of the home guard officer or if he is facing you then it is the same as red light).

646.s: What does this sign on the road indicate?
646.q1: I have a right hand give way duty in the junction further ahead.
646.q2: I have an absolute give way duty in the junction further ahead.
646.q3: I have to give way to traffic from both left and right sides in the junction further ahead.

647.s: You are driving at about 30-40 km/h and you would like to continue straight ahead. How will you continue?
647.q1: I pay special attention to the lorry's maneuverabilities.
647.q2: I continue with the same or almost same speed of 30-40 km/h.
647.q4: I will give enough space to the oncoming vehicle to finish his maneuver before I continue my driving.
647.e1: Yes, the lorry is turning right and needs a lot of space for his maneuver.

648.s: You are about to enter the roundabout. What should you pay special attention to here?
648.q1: I have an unconditional give way duty.
648.q2: I have to give way to potencial cars and motorbikes on my left.
648.q3: I have to give way to potencial cyclists and mopeds on my left and right sides.
648.q4: If it is free I will enter the roundabout right away.
648.e1: Yes. When you enter a roundabout, you always have an unconditional give way duty.
648.e3: Yes, there is a double way cycle-path.

649.s: You are driving at about 35-40km/h and started overtaking the slow moving vehicle. How will you continue?
649.q1: I speed up and overtake the green car.
649.q2: I continue with the same speed and continue with overtaking.
649.q4: I have to give way to traffic from the side road.
649.e1: No, you must not overtake here. You have to obey right hand give way duty.
649.e4: Yes, there is a road on your right and you have to obey right hand give way duty.

650.s: You are driving at 50 km/h. How will you continue?
650.q2: I stay in the middle of my lane.
650.q3: I move to the right edge of the road.
650.q4: I move all the way to the grass and stop there.
650.e4: Yes, the road is narrow and you have to move into the grass and hold for the oncoming vehicle.

651.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
651.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
651.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here, for 2-3 minutes.
651.e2: No. Stopping or parking must not take place in such a place or in such a way that there is danger or inconvenience to traffic.

652.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
652.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.

653.q2: I am allowed to park the car here for 5 hours.
653.q3: I am allowed to park the car here for only one hour.
653.e3: No. There are no restrictions on Sundays.

654.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
654.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
654.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here, for 2-3 minutes.
654.q3: If I am loading or unloading some goods, then I may stop the car here for many hours.
654.e2: No. There should be minimum of 10 meters distance to the cyclepath.

655.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
655.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
655.e1: Yes. You are allowed to park the car like this on small roads.

656.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
656.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
656.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
656.q3: If I am loading or unloading some goods, then I may stop the car here for many hours.
656.e3: Yes. If you are unloading or loading some goods, then it is stopping but not parking.

657.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
657.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
657.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
657.q3: Getting in and out of the car is allowed.

658.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
658.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
658.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here, for 2-3 minutes.
658.q3: If I am loading or unloading some goods, then I may stop the car here for many hours.

659.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
659.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
659.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
659.e1: No. You will block the parked cars that are on your right. But stopping is allowed.

660.s: You have just left the white car. It is 5 pm, on a Monday evening. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
660.q1: I am allowed to park the car here for two hours.
660.q2: I am allowed to park the car here for 5 hours.
660.q3: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
660.e1: Yes. Until 18:00 parking is limited for one hour. After 18:00 you can park until 8 am next day.

661.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
661.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
661.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

662.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
662.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
662.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
662.q3: If I am loading or unloading some goods, then stopping is unlimited.
662.e3: Yes. Until you have finish unloading.

663.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
663.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
663.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
663.e2: Yes. There are only warning lines here and therefore parking is allowed here.

664.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
664.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
664.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

665.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
665.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
665.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

666.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
666.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
666.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

667.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
667.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
667.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

668.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

669.s: You have just left the white car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
669.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
669.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
669.e2: No, it is too close to the bend.

670.s: You have just left the red car here. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
670.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
670.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
670.q3: If I am loading or unloading some goods, than I may stop the car here for many hours.
670.e2: No. The car should be a minimum of 3 meters away from the continuous line and 10 meters from the junction.

671.s: You have just left the gray car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
671.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
671.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here, for 2-3 minutes.
671.e2: No. The distance between the car and beginning of continues line must be a minimum of 5 meters.

672.s: You have just left the gray car. It is 08:00 am on Friday. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
672.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
672.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
672.q3: It is forbidden to stop the car here.

673.s: You have just left the silver car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
673.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
673.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.

674.s: You have just left the silver car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
674.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
674.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
674.e1: No. There should be minimum of 3 meters distance between the car and the continuous line.

675.s: You are driving at about 60 km/h. How will you continue?
675.q1: I pay special attention to the oncoming traffic.
675.q4: I reduce my speed and stay as far to the right as possible in my lane.
675.e1: Yes. The oncoming car is blinding you.
675.e2: Yes, the oncoming car is blinding you.

676.s: What are the rules about driving with goods?
676.q1: The car with goods must not be longer than 10 meters.
676.q2: The car with goods must not be longer than 12 meters.
676.q3: Goods that protrude more than 15 cm beyond the sides of the vehicle must be marked.
676.q4: If the goods are protruding more than 1 meter behind or in front, then they must be marked.
676.e1: No. The car with goods must not be longer than 12 metres, and can be, for example, 10, 11 or 12 metres.
676.e4: Yes. With a cloth or in some other clearly visible manner. However, in the case of commercial transport, the goods must be marked with a white cylinder 30 cm high and with a diameter of 10 cm. The cylinder must be fitted with two red reflective bands. During the hours when lights must be used, the goods must be marked with the aforementioned cylinder and a red light at the rear and a white light at the front, regardless of whether they are being transported privately or commercially. (see page 67 in the book)

677.s: What should you pay special attention to here?
677.q4: I pay special attention to the potencial traffic coming, from the left and right sides.
677.e3: No. The cyclist does not have an impact on your driving right now.

678.s: You are driving at about 60 km/h. How will you continue?
678.q1: I continue with the same speed of 60 km/h.
678.q2: I cross the broken lines to flatten the bend.
678.q4: I keep my lane through the bend.
678.e1: No. Because of the sharp bend.
678.e2: No. You must not cross the broken lines here.

679.s: You are driving at 50 km/h. The traffic light has just changed to yellow. How will you continue?
679.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic light.
679.q4: I continue at the same speed.
679.e4: Yes. You are too close and you will continue with the same speed.

680.s: You have just left the black car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
680.q1: I am allowed to stop the car here, for 2-3 minutes.
680.q2: I am allowed to park the car here.
680.e1: No. The car is parked on the wrong side of the road. The car is allowed to park on the "wrong" side if the road is one-way and on small residential roads.

681.s: You have left the black car here. It is 10 AM on Saturday. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
681.q1: I am allowed to park the car here for 6 hours.
681.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
681.e1: Yes. Parking is limited to 4 hours only from Monday to Friday but not Saturday and Sunday.

682.s: You have just left the red car. What are the rules about stopping and parking here?
682.q1: I am allowed to park the car here.
682.q2: I am allowed to stop the car here for 2-3 minutes.
682.q3: I am allowed to load and unload passengers or goods for an unlimited amount of time.
682.e2: No. Solid/unbroken yellow kerb line means no stopping. Punctured/broken yellow kerb line means no parking (but stopping allowed).

683.s: You would like to continue straight ahead in this junction. How will you continue?
683.q1: Is it forbidden to overtake here.
683.q3: I pay special attention to the cyclists.
683.q4: I pay special attention to the traffic light.
683.e1: No. You may overtake on the right when there are vehicles wanting to turn left.
683.e3: Yes. You must not come too close to the cyclists.

684.s: You would like to overtake the red car, whom is holding still. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
684.q1: Is it forbidden to overtake here.
684.q3: I pay special attention to the cyclists.
684.e1: No, it is permitted to overtake on the right if the vehicle in front is turning left.
684.e2: Yes. There is no one behind you.

685.s: You are driving at 50 km/h. How will you continue?
685.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic sign.
685.q3: I look behind and if it is free, I will overtake the cyclist with a good side distance.
685.e1: No. You are still allowed to overtake the cyclist.
685.e2: No. You have to check, if it is free from behind.
685.e3: Yes. There are warning lines but no oncoming traffic and there is room to overtake.

686.s: You are driving at about 30 km/h. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
686.q1: I continue with the same, or almost the same speed of 30km/h.
686.q2: I cross the lines and overtake the riders, straight away.
686.q3: I warn the riders with the horn signal.
686.q4: I brake and stay behind the riders.
686.e2: No. You must not cross the continuous lines.

687.s: What should you pay special attention to here?
687.q3: Traffic from the side roads has to give way to me.
687.q4: Traffic from the side road has difficulties to respect their duty.
687.e2: Yes. This is what the sign indicates.
687.e3: Yes. This is what the sign indicates.
687.e4: Yes. That is the warning of the sign.

688.s: What is the maximum speed after these signs?
688.q4: I pay special attention to that I am driving in a built-up area.

689.s: You would like to turn to the left at this junction. How will you continue?
689.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic light.
689.q2: I will move all the way to the left and from there I will turn left.
689.q3: I position myself as far left as possible towards the centre of the carriageway.
689.e2: No. This is not a one way road.
689.e3: Yes. You should position yourself as far left as possible towards the centre of the carriageway (on the right side of the road up to the barrier line in your lane).

690.s: You would like to continue straight ahead in this junction. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
690.q2: I pay special attention to that I have to turn left.
690.q3: I change my lane right away.
690.q4: I pay special attention to the road markings.
690.e1: No. You are allowed to change lane here (before continues line).
690.e2: No. You can still change your lane.

691.s: You would like to continue straight ahead. How will you continue?
691.q1: I pay special attention to the traffic sign.
691.q2: I have to turn left or right in this junction.
691.q4: I pay special attention to the cyclist.
691.e1: No. The sign has no impact on your driving.

692.s: You would like to continue straight ahead. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
692.q1: I pay special attention to the road markings.
692.q2: I change to the lane beside me, right away.
692.q3: I pay special attention to the potential cyclist from behind.
692.e2: No. You must not cross the continuous lines.
692.e3: Yes. You are turning right here.

693.s: You would like to continue straight ahead in this junction. There is no one behind you. How will you continue?
693.q1: I continue driving in my lane.
693.q2: I pay special attention to that I have to turn to the right soon.
693.q3: I change my lane right away.
693.q4: I pay special attention to the road markings.
693.e1: No. You are allowed to change lane here (before continuous lines).
693.e4: Yes. If you continue in the same lane then you have to turn to the right from this lane.

694.s: You would like to overtake the black car, that is turning left. How will you continue?
694.q1: I pay special attention to the cyclists, coming from behind, on my right side.
694.q2: If it is free from behind, I will overtake the black car, on its right side.
694.q3: If it is free from behind, I will overtake the black car, on its left side.
694.q4: I stay behind the black car.
694.e1: Yes. If the lane on your right is not a special lane (bus lane, cycle lane, turn lane) than you are allowed to cross the edge line on your right side and overtake the green car on his right side.

695.s: You are driving at 50 km/h in a built-up area. How will you continue?
695.q1: I pay special attention to the car from the side road.
695.q2: I continue at the same or almost the same speed of 50 km/h.

1045.q4: I continue straight ahead and I will find a better place to turn the car around.

1046.e3: No. Here is a good view.

1048.q2: I overtake the moped with a good side distance.
1048.q4: I will stay behind the moped.

1049.e3: Yes. There have to be at least 3 meters between the continuous line and the car.

1050.q1: I am especially aware of the traffic lights.
1050.q2: I will continue in the same lane.
1050.q3: I will change to the lane on my left.
1050.e2: No. You have to change to the lane on your left.

1051.q1: I am particularly aware of the cyclist.
1051.q2: I am particularly aware of the bend.
1051.q3: I overtake the cyclist with good side distance.
1051.q4: I slow down and wait to overtake the cyclist.
1051.e1: Yes. You are driving on a one-way road  and you are allowed to overtake the cyclist with good side distance. Traffic sign means overtaking forbiden, but the ban does not apply to overtake two-wheeler and two-wheeled small moped.
1051.e2: No. You are driving on a one-way road  and you are allowed to overtake the cyclist with good side distance even when you are driving in a bend. Traffic sign means overtaking forbiden, but the ban does not apply to overtake two-wheeler and two-wheeled small moped.
1051.e4: No. You are driving on a one-way road  and you are allowed to overtake the cyclist with good side distance. Traffic sign means overtaking forbiden, but the ban does not apply to overtake two-wheeler and two-wheeled small moped.

1052.s: You are driving about 30 km/h and would like to continue straight ahead. The car in front of you is holding still. There is a free rear view. How will you continue?
1052.q1: I move further to the left to the middle of the road to get ready to overtake.
1052.q2: I brake and stay behind the dark car.
1052.q3: I cross the edge line on my right and overtake the dark car on his right side.
1052.e1: No, here you have to overtake the vehicle in front of you on his right side, because the car turns left and the lane to the right is not a special lane.
1052.e2: No, you are allowed to overtake here.

1053.s: You are driving 40 km/h, same as the oncoming car. There is a free rear view. How will you continue?
1053.q1: I move as far as possible to the right side of the roadway.
1053.q2: I continue at the same speed 40 km/h.
1053.q3: I brake and hold back for the oncoming car.
1053.e1: Yes, oncoming vehicle is approaching in your lane.
1053.e2: No, you need to be critical and expect that the oncoming will not hold back for you even if obstacle is in his lane.
1053.e3: Yes, the oncoming car drive with 40 km/h and and is on its way in your lane, so give way for him.

1054.s: You are driving outside of a built-up area and have caught up with two cars with campers that drive about 60 km/h. There is a free rear view. How will you continue?
1054.q2: I overtake both cars with campers.
1054.q3: I overtake only one car with camper.
1054.q4: I slow down and wait to overtake.
1054.e1:
No, there is no need to flash with the headlights right now and you have to stay behind and wait to overtake.
There is poor visibility and in the picture it is difficult to see if there is an oncoming car or not, therefore you must be critical and wait with overtaking.
1054.e2: No, there is poor visibility and in the picture it is difficult to see if there is an oncoming car or not, therefore you must be critical and not overtake right now.
1054.e3: No, there is poor visibility and in the picture it is difficult to see if there is an oncoming car or not, therefore you must be critical and not overtake right now.

1055.s: You would like to continue straight ahead. What will you be especially aware of here?
1055.q1: I have a give-way duty to the right in this junction.
1055.q2: I am especially aware of that I have to wait only for traffic from my right.
1055.q3: I have an unconditional give-way duty in this junction.
1055.q4: I am especially aware of that I have to wait for traffic from both my left and right side.

1056.s: You would like to turn left in this junction. How will you continue?
1056.q1: The car on my left should drive first.
1056.q3: The oncoming car should drive first.
1056.q4: The oncoming car should drive first, then me and the last car will be the car on my left.
1056.e4: Yes. The car on your left should give way to both sides, you are crossing oncoming car`s direction and you have to wait for him before you turn left.

1057.s: You are driving at 90 km/h on an entrance lane to a motorway.  How will you continue?
1057.q1: I continue at the same speed.
1057.q3: I pay special attention to the traffic coming from behind on my right side.
1057.q4: I pay special attention to the traffic coming from behind on my left side.
1057.e1: No, you have to speed up.
1057.e3: No. You are driving in the entrance lane.

1058.s: You are driving with the low beam on. The oncoming car is blinding you. How will you continue?
1058.q2: I continue with the low beam on.
1058.e1: No. You will blind the driver in front of you.
1058.e3: No. You will blind the driver in front of you.

1059.s: You are driving 70 km/h. How will you continue?
1059.q1: I continue with the same speed of 70 km/h.
1059.q2: I am especially aware of possible obstacles ahead.
1059.q4: I move to the right before the top.
1059.e1: No. Because you are approaching the top and it will be too fast.
1059.e4: Yes. You should move to the right on narrow roads before the top.

1060.s: What are the rules for driving with a registered trailer?
1060.q1: After the road sign the maximum speed is 50 km/h.
1060.q2: After the road sign the maximum speed is 60 km/h.
1060.q3: After the road sign the maximum speed is 70 km/h.
1060.q4: After the road sign the maximum speed is 80 km/h.
1060.e3: No. After the 1/1-20 the new limit is 80 km/h.
1060.e4: Yes. After the 1/1-20 the new limit is 80 km/h.

1061.s: You are driving 70 km/h and cathing up with the tractor. The tractor has moved a bit to the right. There is a free rare view. How will you continue?
1061.q1: I will flash the lights to the tractor.
1061.q2: I speed up to 80 km/h and overtake the tractor.
1061.q3: I continue with the same speed 70 km/h and overtake the tractor.
1061.q4: I reduce my speed and wait to overtake the tractor.
1061.e1: No. You may not overtake the tractor now. There is a poor view and there is a motorcycle oncoming.
1061.e2: No. There is a poor view and there is a motorcycle oncoming.
1061.e3: No. There is a poor view and there is a motorcycle oncoming.

1062.s: You have taken the wrong way and want to turn around as soon as possible. There is a free rear view. What will you do?
1062.q1: I will turn around right away.
1062.q2: I continue on to the parking area and turn around when the lorry has passed.
1062.q3: I am especially aware of the solid lines.
1062.q4: I am especially aware of the oncoming lorry.
1062.e1: No.  There are solid lines and you have to find a different place to turn.
1062.e2: No.  There are solid lines and you have to find a different place to turn.
1062.e3: Yes. The solid line is not allowed to be crosed.
1062.e4: No. The lorry has no impact on your driving right now.

1063.s: You are driving 40 km/h. How will you continue?
1063.q1: I continue with the same speed.
1063.q2: I expect the tractor to wait for me.
1063.q3: I move all the way to the fence.
1063.q4: I brake and I am ready to come to a stop.
1063.e1: No. The road is narrow and the tractor needs a lot of space.
1063.e2: No, you must be ready to brake for the tractor
1063.e3: No, there is too much mud.

1064.s: You're driving 50 km/h. How will you continue?
1064.q1: I continue at the same speed.
1064.q3: I reduce my speed to 40 km/h.
1064.e2: Yes, because the oncoming car dazzles you.
1064.e3: Yes. Always adjust the speed to the low beam range and be prepared to halt.

1065.s: You are driving 40km/h. How will you continue?
1065.q1: I am especially aware of the oncoming bus.
1065.q2: I continue at the same speed.
1065.q3: I move as far as possible to the right.
1065.q4: I slow down and I'm ready to stop.
1065.e1: Yes. The road is narrow and you must slow down and be prepared to stop.
1065.e4: Yes. Because of the narrow road.

1066.s: You are driving 45-50 km/h. How will you continue?
1066.q1: I continue with the same speed.
1066.q3: I move to the middle of the road.
1066.q4: I stop and wait for the pedestrians.
1066.e1: No, you need to hold back for pedestrians who are in the pedestrian zone or on their way to cross the pedestrian zone.
1066.e2: No. You need to slow down and hold back for pedestrians from both sides and you should not move to the right or towards the middle of the road.
1066.e3: No. You need to slow down and hold back for pedestrians from both sides and you should not move towards the middle of the road.

1067.s: You are driving 70 km/h. The car in front of you drive slowly. How will you proceed?
1067.q1: I speed up to 80 km/t and overtake the black car.
1067.q2: I continue with the same speed and overtake the black car.
1067.q4: I stay behind and overtake later.
1067.e1: No. The speed limit is 70 km/h and you may not drive 80 km/h here.
1067.e3: No, you can overtake the car.
1067.e4: No, you can overtake the car.

1068.s: You want to turn right in this junction. What will you be particularly aware of here?
1068.q1: Right-hand give-way duty applies in this junction.
1068.q2: Unconditional give-way duty applies in this junction.
1068.q3: I have to give way to traffic on my left.
1068.q4: I am especially aware of the person's age.
1068.e3: No. The right-hand give-way duty applies here and traffic from your left is supposed to wait for you.
1068.e4: Yes, because children can react unexpectedly.

1069.s: You are exiting a parking area and want to turn left. It is free on your right side. How will you continue?
1069.q1: The rule of unconditional give-way duty applies here.
1069.q2: The rule of right-hand give-way duty applies here.
1069.q3: I expect that the cyclist will let me drive first.
1069.q4: I will wait for the cyclist.
1069.e1: Yes, always when exiting a parking area.
1069.e3: No, you must wait for the cyclist to pass.
1069.e4: Yes, the cyclist is close to you and you have to wait.

1070.s: What are the rules for driving under the influence of alcohol?
1070.q1: You may drive if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is 0.51.
1070.q2: You may drive if your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is 0.81.
1070.q3: You may drive with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.3, even if you are unable to drive safely.
1070.q4: Handing your car over to someone who has consumed so much alcohol that they are unable to drive safely is a criminal offence.
1070.e1: No, the limit is 0.5 and if it is higher then driving is illegal.
1070.e2: No, the limit is 0.5 and if it is higher then driving is illegal.
1070.e3: No, if you cant't drive safely or are involved in an accident, then you can be convicted for driving under the influence of alcohol, eventhough your BAC is below 0.5.

1071.s: What vehicles are you allowed to drive with catecory b-drivers license?
1071.q1: Passenger car and light commercial vehicle of 3,800 kilos permissible total weight.
1071.q2: Passenger car and light commercial vehicle of 3,500 kilos allowed total weight.
1071.q3: Car towing a trailer with a maximum allowed weight not exceeding 750 kilos.
1071.q4: Car of 2,600 kilos allowed total weight and trailer of 1,000 kilos allowed total weight.
1071.e1: No, not over 3,500 kg/kilos allowed total weight.
1071.e2: Yes, not over 3,500 kg/kilos allowed total weight.
1071.e3: Yes. As long as the car is appoved to tower that weight.
1071.e4: No, a car with a towed vehicle with a permissible total weight exceeding 750 kilos, provided that the car and the trailer together do not exceed 3,500 kg permissible total weight. Here the total 'allowable total weight' = 3,600 kilos, ie. 100 kilos too much.

1072.s: What applies the first 3 years for the first-time b-drivers license acquirer?
1072.q1: Your drivers license will be revoked at the third clip.
1072.q2: Your drivers license will be revoked at the second clip.
1072.q3: Your drivers license will be revoked at the first clip.
1072.q4: If the drivers license is revoked, special teaching is required before a new driving exam.
1072.e1: No. The drivers license is already revoked with the second clip. (Only when the drivers license is older than 3 years, will the license be revoked at the third clip).
1072.e2: Yes. The drivers license is revoked at the second clip.
1072.e4: Yes, 8 theory lessons ans 8 driving lessons with an approved driving instructor.

1073.s: At what speeding will you recieve a clip in your drivers license?
1073.q1: If the speeding is higher than 30% of the allowed speed.
1073.q2: If the speeding is higher than 25% of the allowed speed.
1073.q3: If the speeding is higher than 20% of the allowed speed.
1073.e1: Yes, this will give a clip.

1074.s: Which of the following conditions revokes drivers licence for a first-time acquirer?
1074.q1: By driving at 150 km/h on the motorway.
1074.q2: By driving at 160 km/h on the motorway.
1074.q3: Driving faster than speed limits with more than 50%.
1074.q4: Driving faster than speed limits with more than 60%.
1074.e1: No, by driving at 160 km/h or faster on the motorway?
1074.e2: Yes, by driving at 160 km/h or faster on the motorway?
1074.e3: No, it is at 60% on roads (roads other than motorway).
1074.e4: Yes, it is at 60% on roads (roads other than motorway).

1075.s: At which of the following conditions will you get a clip in your driver's license?
1075.q1: When driving with a BAC of 0.7.
1075.q2: When driving opposite direction of a one-way road.
1075.q3: When passing a traffic island on the left side.
1075.q4: When driving over railroad crossing when the stop signal has been given.
1075.e1: No, but you will receive conditional clearance of your driver's license.
1075.e3: Yes, always pass on the right side. Only if it is indicated by a traffic sign or it is a one-way road, can you choose the left side.

1452.q1: The driver is responsible for ensuring that the vehicle is in a safe condition.
1452.q2: The owner or registered user is responsible for ensuring that the car is in legal condition.
1452.q3: The driver must always be aware that the car is in good working order, especially that the steering, brakes, lights and horn are working safely and according to legal requirements.
1452.q4: Only the owner of the car is responsible for ensuring that the car is in a safe condition.
1452.e1: The owner or registered user is responsible for the car being in legal condition and the driver is responsible for the car being in a safe condition.
1452.e2: The owner or registered user is responsible for the car being in legal condition and the driver is responsible for the car being in a safe condition.
1452.e3: The driver must always be aware that the vehicle is in good working order and in particular that the steering, brakes, lights and audible signalling device (horn) are working safely and according to legal requirements. (When driving with a trailer, make sure that the coupling is secure).
1452.e4: No. The owner or registered user is responsible for the car being in legal condition and the driver is responsible for the car being in a safe condition.

1454.s: What are the rules for the steering gear?
1454.q1: The steering system must be designed so that the car can be steered slowly and sluggishly.
1454.q2: The steering system must be designed in such a way that the car can be steered easily, safely and quickly.
1454.q3: There must be significant play in the steering system as a whole or in its individual parts.
1454.q4: There must be no significant play in the steering system as a whole or in its individual parts due to wear or similar.
1454.e1: No. The steering system must be designed so that the car can be steered easily and safely. The steering system must be designed so that the car can be steered easily, safely and quickly.
1454.e2: Yes. Styreapparatet skal være således indrettet, at bilen kan styres let, sikkert og hurtigt.
1454.e4: Yes. There must be no significant play in the steering system as a whole or in its individual parts due to wear or similar.

1455.s: What are the signs of a failure in the steering system?
1455.q1: Heavy or difficult steering can be caused by a lack of fluid in the power steering reservoir, a worn or broken power steering drive belt or a fault in the electric power steering system.
1455.q2: If the wheels do not immediately follow the movement of the steering wheel, it may be a sign of slack in the steering connections.
1455.q3: If the wheels do not immediately follow the movement of the steering wheel, this may indicate a brake fault.
1455.q4: The steering system must be inspected if there is too little fluid in the servo system or if there is significant steering wheel play.
1455.e1: Yes. Heavy or difficult steering can be caused by a lack of fluid in the power steering reservoir, a worn or broken power steering drive belt or a fault in the electric power steering system.
1455.e3: NO. If the wheels do not immediately follow the movement of the steering wheel, this may be a sign of play in the steering connections.

1456.s: What rules apply to car brakes?
1456.q1: The service brake must work on only 2 wheels.
1456.q2: The parking brake must be able to keep the car stopped on an inclined road.
1456.q3: The service brake must work on all wheels and be able to brake the vehicle safely, quickly and effectively at all speeds and loads.
1456.q4: The parking brake is allowed to be inoperative.
1456.e1: No. The service brake must work on all wheels and be able to brake the vehicle safely, quickly and effectively at all speeds and loads.
1456.e3: Yes. The service brake must work on all wheels and be able to brake the vehicle safely, quickly and effectively at all speeds and loads.
1456.e4: No. The parking brake must be able to keep the car stopped on an inclined road.

1457.q1: The car pulls askew under light braking on a level road.
1457.q2: The brake pedal is suddenly pressed down further than usual.
1457.q4: The brake pedal shakes when braking hard.
1457.e1: Yes. If the vehicle pulls to the side when braking lightly on a level road, this indicates a fault in the brake system or moisture or dirt on the brake pads. Moisture can penetrate the brakes during a car wash, for example, but will disappear after braking for a short time.
1457.e2: Yes. If the brake pedal can suddenly be depressed further than usual, it is a sign that one brake circuit is defective.
1457.e3: Yes. Uneven braking or sudden chopping from one or more wheels indicates faults in brake drums, brake discs or brake linings.
1457.e4: No. This is a sign that the ABS braking system is activated. (anti-lock braking system)

1458.s: In which situation(s) do you need to inspect the brakes immediately?
1458.q1: If there is too little brake fluid in the brake fluid reservoir or if the indicator light comes on while driving.
1458.q2: If the brake pedal can be pressed down further than normal.
1458.q3: If the braking is uneven or the car pulls to the side during braking.
1458.q4: If the indicator light for the ABS braking system goes out shortly after starting.
1458.e1: Yes. Brakes should be inspected immediately if there is too little brake fluid in the brake fluid reservoir, if the indicator light comes on while driving, if the brake pedal can be depressed further than normal, or if braking is uneven or the vehicle pulls to the side while braking.
1458.e4: No. The indicator light should go out shortly after switching on the car. If the indicator light for the ABS braking system does not go out shortly after switching on, this indicates a fault in the ABS braking system and only driving to the nearest repair garage is permitted.

1459.s: What are the rules for lights and reflectors?
1459.q1: The vehicle may only be equipped with mandatory or permitted lights and reflectors.
1459.q2: All lights and reflectors must be intact, clean and undamaged.
1459.q3: Only low and high beams must be whole, clean and undamaged.
1459.q4: The headlight light should be white or yellowish.
1459.e1: Yes. The vehicle may only be equipped with mandatory or permitted lights and reflectors.
1459.e2: Yes. All lights and reflectors must be intact, clean and undamaged.

1460.s: Which of these lights and reflectors are mandatory?
1460.q2: Two lights with asymmetric low beam.
1460.e3: No. They are permitted but not mandatory. The permitted lights and reflectors include: additional main beam headlights, daytime running lights, additional stop lights, additional tail lights, front fog lights, reversing lights, rear fog lights, search lights, work lights, marker lights, parking lights and overtaking lights, for which special rules apply. Furthermore, the car may be equipped with white reflectors at the front, yellow reflectors on the sides and additional red reflectors at the rear.
1460.e4:
Yes. The mandatory lights and reflectors include:
a) two headlamps with high beam,
b) two lamps with asymmetrical dipped beam,
c) two lights with position light,
d) two lights with rear lights,
e) three lamps with stop lights (older cars can have only two stop lights),
f) at least one licence plate light,
g) two indicators at the front and rear of the car and one on each side of the car; and
h) two red approved and labelled rear reflectors (must not be triangular).

1461.s: Which of the following rules apply to lights and reflectors?
1461.q1: High beam (long beam) must be able to illuminate the road at least 300 metres in front of the car.
1461.q2: High beam (the long light) must be able to illuminate the road at least 100 metres in front of the car.
1461.q3: The dipped beam must be able to illuminate the road at least 30 metres in front of the car without glare.
1461.q4: The position light must be clearly visible from at least 300 metres away without blinding glare.
1461.e1: No. The high beam of the headlights must be able to illuminate the road at least 100 metres in front of the car, the low beam must be able to illuminate the road at least 30 metres in front of the car without glare, and the position light must be clearly visible at least 300 metres away without blinding.
1461.e3: Yes. The low beam must be able to illuminate the road at least 30 metres in front of the vehicle without glare.
1461.e4: Yes. The main beam (high beam) of the headlights must be able to illuminate the road at least 100 metres in front of the vehicle, the low beam must be able to illuminate the road at least 30 metres in front of the vehicle without glare, and the position light must be clearly visible at least 300 metres away without glare7blinding.

1462.s: Which of the following rules apply to lights and reflectors?
1462.q1: The headlight light should be white or yellowish.
1462.q2: The rear light should be white or yellowish.
1462.q3: All lights and reflectors must be whole, clean and undamaged.
1462.q4: Cars longer than 6 metres must be equipped with yellow side reflectors and side marker lights.
1462.e1: Yes. The headlight light should be white or yellowish.
1462.e2: No. The rear light must be red.
1462.e3: Yes. All lights and reflectors must be intact, clean and undamaged.
1462.e4: Yes. Cars longer than 6 metres must be fitted with approved and labelled amber side reflectors and side marker lights distributed on the sides of the car.

1463.s: What does it mean if the indicators flash significantly faster than usual?
1463.q1: This is a sign that I have switched on the hazard lights.
1463.q2: This is a sign that the car's automatic indicators are activated.
1463.q3: This is usually a sign that one or more indicators are not working.
1463.q4: This is a sign that the ABS system is activated.
1463.e1: No, it isn't. If the indicators are flashing significantly faster than usual, this is usually a sign that one or more indicators are not working.
1463.e3: Yes. If the indicators are flashing significantly faster than usual, it is usually a sign that one or more indicators are not working.
1463.e4: No. If you brake hard, some car models will automatically activate hazard lights, but they will not flash faster than usual.

1464.s: What rules apply to the horn?
1464.q2: The horn is allowed to have melodies.
1464.q3: The horn should have a clear, constant tone.
1464.q4: I may use the horn to greet my friends or at weddings.
1464.e1: No. You should always make sure there is a working horn in the car and the horn should have a clear, constant tone.
1464.e2: No. The horn should have a clear, constant tone.
1464.e4: No. When it is necessary to warn of a danger, make others aware of the danger by briefly sounding the horn or flashing the headlights. Use of the horn in other cases is prohibited. Using the horn with small children should be done with caution as it can easily provoke panic reactions.

1465.s: In which of the following situations should you signal with your indicator?
1465.q1: Before starting from the edge of the carriageway, before turnaround and before left- or right-turning.
1465.q2: Before changing lanes on the motorway and any other not insignificant change of the vehicle's position to the side, including when entering and exiting the motorway.
1465.q3: Before I start reversing I always have to flash to the right.
1465.q4: Before entering a roundabout to be exited by the first side road, signal right.
1465.e2: Yes. Always signal before changing lanes on motorways. The same applies to any other not insignificant change in the vehicle's position to the side, including when entering and exiting a motorway. On other roads, you must signal when required to guide other traffic.
1465.e4: Yes. Before approaching a roundabout to be exited by the first side road, signal to the right. If the roundabout is to be exited by the last side road, you may signal to the left. When exiting a roundabout after the first side road, signposting starts to the right of the centre of the side road before the exit you want to use.

1466.s: What rules apply to the use of hazard lights?
1466.q1: If I stop or park, I can use the hazard warning light to be extra visible.
1466.q2: In addition to the warning triangle, hazard flashers can be used.
1466.q3: In case of unexpected queues or other immediate danger, hazard flashers must be used on motorways. On other roads outside of densely built-up areas, hazard flashers can be used.
1466.q4: When towing another vehicle I need to use hazard lights.
1466.e1:
No. It is forbidden to use the hazard warning signal when stopping and parking. 
In the event of a breakdown, accident or similar in a place where stopping or parking is prohibited, you must move the car away from the place as soon as possible and on motorways as far away from the carriageway as possible. If the car is a danger or inconvenience to traffic, an approved warning triangle must be placed immediately at least 50 metres before the car on ordinary roads and at least 100 metres before the car on motorways. In addition to the warning triangle, hazard warning lights can be used.
In the event of unexpected queues or other immediate danger on motorways and roads outside densely built-up areas, hazard warning lights may (on motorways must) be used to draw other road users' attention to the danger.
 The use of hazard warning lights in other cases is prohibited.
1466.e2: Yes. In the event of a breakdown, accident or similar in a place where stopping or parking is prohibited, the vehicle must be moved away from the place as soon as possible and, on motorways, as far as possible completely off the roadway. If the car is a danger or inconvenience to traffic, an approved warning triangle must be placed immediately at least 50 metres before the car on ordinary roads and at least 100 metres before the car on motorways. In addition to the warning triangle, hazard warning lights can be used.
1466.e4:
No. It is permitted to use the vehicle to tow a damaged car, tractor or motorised implement under certain conditions. The towing must be done using a solid rope, a pole connection or similar and so that the distance between the vehicles is no more than 4 m. If the distance is more than 2 m, the rope must be clearly marked. The towed vehicle must be driven by a person who has a driving licence for the vehicle. The speed must not exceed 30 km/h.
Towing is prohibited if the towed vehicle's brakes or steering equipment are not in proper working order, in which case the towing must be entrusted to an authorised recovery vehicle or similar. Towing on motorways may only be carried out with an approved recovery vehicle.

1467.s: What are the energy and eco-driving rules?
1467.q1: To minimise air and noise pollution, avoid leaving the engine idling for long periods of time.
1467.q2: To minimise air and noise pollution, start the engine well in advance so it warms up before you start driving.
1467.q3: Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1467.q4: Driving with under-inflated tyres reduces energy consumption.
1467.e1: Yes. To minimise air and noise pollution, avoid leaving the engine idling for long periods of time.
1467.e2: No. To minimise air and noise pollution, you should not leave the engine idling for long periods of time. Many municipalities have a rule that you should not idle the engine for more than 1 minute.
1467.e3: Yes. Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1467.e4: No. Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.

1468.s: What are the rules for energy and eco-driving?
1468.q1: Driving behaviour has little impact on energy consumption.
1468.q2: Driving behaviour has a major impact on energy consumption.
1468.q3: Energy efficient driving is generally understood to mean making many unnecessary and repetitive speed changes.
1468.q4: Energy consumption is reduced if the engine is switched off automatically when stopping.
1468.e1: No. High speeds and aggressive driving with heavy acceleration, for example when overtaking, lead to increased fuel consumption, while energy-efficient driving techniques can generally result in 5-10% fuel savings and in many cases up to 25% savings.
1468.e3: No. Energy-efficient driving means generally avoiding unnecessary and repetitive speed changes.
1468.e4: Yes. Energy consumption is reduced if the engine is switched off automatically when stopping.

1469.s: How can you reduce energy consumption?
1469.q1: When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as long as possible.
1469.q2: When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by fully releasing the accelerator and then disengaging the clutch.
1469.q3: By choosing as high a gear as possible, energy consumption is reduced.
1469.q4: By choosing as low a gear as possible, energy consumption is reduced.
1469.e1: Yes. When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as long as possible.
1469.e2: No. When reducing speed, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as much as possible.
1469.e4: No. By choosing as high a gear as possible, energy consumption is reduced.

1470.s: How can you reduce energy consumption for energy and eco-driving?
1470.q1: When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as much as possible.
1470.q2: When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by letting off the accelerator completely and disengaging as soon as possible.
1470.q3: By choosing as low a gear as possible, energy consumption is reduced.
1470.q4: By choosing as high a gear as possible, energy consumption is reduced.

1471.s: How can you reduce energy consumption for energy and eco-driving?
1471.q1: Changing gears late and choosing as low a gear as possible reduces energy consumption.
1471.q2: Changing gears early and choosing as high a gear as possible reduces energy consumption.
1471.q3: Accelerating quickly with the accelerator pedal about halfway down and selecting the correct gear reduces energy consumption.
1471.q4: The correct gear selection may be to shift from, for example, 2nd to 4th or 3rd to 5th gear.
1471.e1: No. Changing gears early and choosing as high a gear as possible reduces energy consumption.
1471.e2: Yes. Changing gears early and choosing as high a gear as possible reduces energy consumption.
1471.e3: Yes. Accelerating quickly with the accelerator pedal about halfway down and making the correct gear selection reduces energy consumption. Correct gear selection can be shifting from 2nd to 4th or 3rd to 5th gear, for example. Changing gears early and selecting as high a gear as possible will reduce energy consumption.
1471.e4: Yes. Accelerating quickly with the accelerator pedal about halfway down and making the correct gear selection reduces energy consumption. Correct gear selection can be shifting from 2nd to 4th or 3rd to 5th gear, for example. Changing gears early and selecting as high a gear as possible will reduce energy consumption.

1472.s: How can you reduce energy consumption related to energy and eco-driving?
1472.q1: Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1472.q2: Driving with over-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1472.q3: Driving with a roof box or similar reduces energy consumption.
1472.q4: When driving with a roof box or similar, energy consumption increases.
1472.e1: Yes. Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1472.e2: No. Driving with under-inflated tyres increases energy consumption.
1472.e3: No. Driving with a roof box or similar increases energy consumption.

1473.s: How can you reduce energy consumption for energy and eco-driving?
1473.q1: Driving with the air conditioning or climate control switched on increases energy consumption.
1473.q2: Driving with the air conditioning or climate control switched on reduces energy consumption.
1473.q3: Energy-efficient driving techniques do not save fuel.
1473.q4: Energy-efficient driving techniques can save up to 25 per cent on fuel.
1473.e1: Yes. Driving with the air conditioning or climate control switched on and other power-consuming equipment increases energy consumption.
1473.e3: No. High speeds and aggressive driving with heavy acceleration, for example when overtaking, lead to increased fuel consumption, while energy-efficient driving techniques can generally result in 5-10% fuel savings and in many cases up to 25% savings.

1474.s: Which statements are correct when it comes to energy and eco-driving?
1474.q1: Loading the vehicle has no impact on energy consumption.
1474.q2: High speeds and aggressive driving with heavy acceleration increase fuel consumption.
1474.q3: Car idling is good for the environment.
1474.q4: Driving with the air conditioning or climate control switched on increases energy consumption.
1474.e1: No. Driving with unnecessary weight in the car increases energy consumption.
1474.e2: Yes. High speeds and aggressive driving with heavy acceleration, for example when overtaking, lead to increased fuel consumption, while energy-efficient driving techniques can generally result in 5-10% fuel savings and in many cases up to 25% savings.
1474.e3: No. To minimise air and noise pollution, do not leave the engine idling for long periods of time.
1474.e4: Yes. Driving with the air conditioning or climate control switched on increases energy consumption.

1475.s: How should you drive when approaching signalised intersections, when you can anticipate that stopping for yellow or red will be necessary?
1475.q1: I have to continue at high speed and brake hard at the end.
1475.q2: I have to adjust my speed for the final stretch towards the junction.
1475.q3: I reduce energy consumption by letting off the accelerator completely and avoid disengaging if possible.
1475.q4: I reduce energy consumption by letting off the accelerator completely and disengaging as soon as possible.
1475.e1: No. When approaching signalised intersections, anticipate whether stopping for yellow or red is necessary, and if so, adjust speed for the final stretch towards the intersection, rather than continuing at high speed and then braking hard at the end.
1475.e3: Yes. When slowing down, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as much as possible.
1475.e4: No. When reducing speed, energy consumption can be reduced by releasing the accelerator completely and avoiding disengaging the clutch as much as possible.

1476.s: Which of the claims about non-use of seatbelts are correct?
1476.q1: The risk of being killed in an accident is many times greater if you are thrown out of the car than if you stay in the car.
1476.q2: 18-24 year old drivers are more often than others involved in rollover accidents.
1476.q3: The car's airbag can be downright deadly when not wearing a seatbelt.
1476.q4: If you're not buckled up, you're often thrown around the car in an accident. The risk of injuring yourself and others in the car is very high.
1476.e2: 18-24 year old drivers are more often than others involved in accidents where the car rolls over and the risk of being ejected is high. In these accidents, the use of seat belts has a particularly high effect.

1477.s: Which of the claims about non-use of seatbelts are correct?
1477.q1: No person can withstand the pressure created in a collision when not wearing a seatbelt.
1477.q2: If you are fit and physically strong, you can withstand the pressure of a collision when not wearing a seatbelt.
1477.q3: You will only receive a fine if passengers under the age of 15 do not wear a seatbelt while driving.
1477.q4: You get a penalty on your driving licence if passengers under the age of 15 do not wear a seatbelt while driving.
1477.e1: Yes. No person can withstand the pressure created by a collision when not wearing a seatbelt. Even at speeds below 10 km/h, you can't resist without a seatbelt.
1477.e3:
No. You also get a penalty point on your driving licence if passengers under the age of 15 do not wear a seatbelt while driving. 
Two penalty points result in a driving ban for first-time licence holders within the first 3 years.
1477.e4:
Yes.  You get a penalty point on your driving licence if passengers under the age of 15 do not wear a seatbelt while driving. 
Two penalty points result in a driving ban for first-time licence holders within the first 3 years.

1478.s: What conditions apply to the steering system?
1478.q1: Lack of fluid in the servo reservoir can cause heavy steering.
1478.q2: There must be significant play in steering connections.
1478.q3: If the wheels do not immediately follow the movement of the steering wheel, it may be a sign of play in the steering connections.
1478.q4: The steering must be checked if there is too little fluid in the servo system.
1478.e1: Yes. eavy or difficult steering may be due to lack of fluid in the servo reservoir, a worn or broken power steering drive belt or a fault in the electric power steering system.
1478.e2: No. There must be no significant play in the steering system as a whole or in its individual parts due to wear or similar.
1478.e3: Yes.  If the wheels do not immediately follow the movement of the steering wheel, this may be a sign of play in the steering connections.
1478.e4: Yes. The steering must be inspected if there is too little fluid in the servo system or if there is significant ratchet play.

1480.s: What are the conditions for consuming alcohol?
1480.q1: You can be penalised for drink driving even if your blood alcohol level is below 0.5 if you cannot drive safely.
1480.q2: You can only be penalised for drink driving if your blood alcohol level is over 0.5 if you cannot drive safely.
1480.q3: Only in the case of road traffic accidents and drink-driving, an ANT course must be completed.
1480.q4: An ANT course must always be completed in connection with drink-driving.
1480.e1: Yes. If you cannot drive safely, you can be penalised for drink driving even if your blood alcohol level is lower than 0.5.
1480.e2: No.  If you cannot drive safely, you can be penalised for drink driving even if your blood alcohol level is lower than 0.5.
1480.e3: No. An ANT course must always be completed in connection with drink-driving.
1480.e4: Yes. An ANT course must always be completed in connection with drink-driving

1483.s: The ABS light turns on while you are driving. What will you do?
1483.q1: Nothing, it is only indicative and does not affect the drive.
1483.q2: I'll have it checked at the next service check in a couple of months.
1483.q3: I drive to the nearest car workshop.
1483.e3: Yes. Only driving to the nearest car workshop is allowed.

1486.s: What do you need to pay special attention to here?
1486.q4: I must pass the obstacle on the right.
1486.e1: No. The traffic sign means mandatory passage direction to the right.
1486.e2: No. The traffic sign means mandatory passage direction to the right.

1487.s: Which of the following laws and conditions are correct?
1487.q1: Only lights with brake lights must be intact, clean and undamaged.
1487.q2: The high beam must be able to illuminate the road at least 100 metres in front of the car.
1487.q3: The position light must be clearly visible from a distance of at least 300 meters without glare.
1487.q4: There must be two lights with asymmetric low beam.
1487.e1: No.  All lights and reflectors must be intact, clean and undamaged.
1487.e2: Yes. The high beam (long beam) must be able to illuminate the road at least 100 metres in front of the car.
1487.e3: Yes. The position light must be clearly visible from at least 300 metres away without glare/dazzling.
1487.e4: Yes. There must be two lights with asymmetric low beam that can illuminate the road at least 30 metres in front of the car without glare

1488.s: What are the rules if you are under the influence of mind-altering substances (drugs and certain medicines) and choose to drive?
1488.q1: Taking drugs and certain medications affects your ability to drive and increases the risk of road accidents.
1488.q2: The use of mind-altering drugs in contravention of a doctor's prescription may be covered by the rules on driving with mind-altering substances in the blood.
1488.q3: The first offence is punishable only by a fine if consciousness-altering substances are found in the blood.
1488.q4: Completing an ANT course is optional when driving under the influence of drugs.
1488.e1: Yes. Taking drugs and certain medications affects your ability to drive and increases the risk of road accidents.
1488.e2: Yes. The use of mind-altering drugs in contravention of a doctor's prescription may be covered by the rules on driving with mind-altering substances in the blood.
1488.e3: No.  The first penalty for the detection of drugs affecting consciousness in the blood is a fine and unconditional disqualification (equivalent to the penalty for driving with a blood alcohol level of 1.21).
1488.e4: No. An ANT course must always be completed when driving with mind-altering substances.

1489.s: What does this road sign mean?
1489.e1: No. The traffic sign means risk of queueing.
1489.e2: No. The traffic sign indicates a risk of traffic jams.
1489.e3: Yes. The traffic sign indicates a risk of traffic jams.
1489.e4: No. The traffic sign indicates a risk of traffic jams.

1490.s: You are driving at 40 km/h and want to turn right at the traffic lights. What do you do?
1490.q1: I continue straight ahead because it is forbidden to turn right.
1490.q2: I slow down a little and turn right in front of the cyclist.
1490.q3: I brake and hold back for the cyclist before turning right.
1490.q4: I pay special attention to the traffic signs.
1490.e1: No. Only trucks are not allowed to turn right.
1490.e2: No. You must brake and hold back for the cyclist.
1490.e3: Yes. You must brake and hold back for the cyclist.
1490.e4: No. You should only pay attention to them and not pay special attention because they have no bearing on your intended manoeuvre. You should focus on the traffic light and the cyclist on your right as well as any other cyclists or pedestrians you want to cross on the road you are entering.

1491.s: What do you do in this situation?
1491.q1: I continue at the same speed of 50 km/h.
1491.q2: I use the horn signal to warn the car in front.
1491.e1: No. The car in front brakes and you also have to brake, but softly because the car behind is close to you.
1491.e2: No. The car in front is already braking and you just need to brake softly.
1491.e3: No,  The car in front brakes and you have to brake too, but brake softly because the car behind is close to you.
1491.e4: Yes. The car in front brakes and you have to brake too, but brake softly because the car behind is close to you.

1492.s: You want to continue straight ahead. What do you need to pay special attention to?
1492.q2: I am entering an area where special traffic rules apply.
1492.q4: I am allowed to continue straight ahead.
1492.e1: No.  There is a sub sign that shows that driving is allowed. Without the sub sign, it will not be allowed to enter a cycle lane.
1492.e2:
Yes. Bicycle street (E 47) indicates an area where special traffic rules apply. Any authorisation for driving is indicated by a sub-board and applies to any special types of traffic. The speed must be adapted to the others in the area, normally max. 30 km/h. Parking in a cycle lane is not permitted outside specially marked spaces.
At the end of the cycle lane (E 48), drivers have an unconditional duty to give way when exiting a cycle lane. You must drive at an appropriately low speed in a cycle lane. When travelling in a cycle lane, drivers must show special care and consideration for each other and must not unnecessarily impede the progress of other drivers.
1492.e3: Yes.   There is a sub sign that shows that driving is allowed. Without the sub sign, it will not be allowed to enter a cycle lane.
1492.e4: Yes.   There is a sub sign that shows that driving is allowed. Without the sub sign, it will not be allowed to enter a cycle lane.
